claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility, I first need to know about the children you're claiming for. 

**How old is your child (or children)?** 

Please tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age or date of birth

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation, as the age of the child is a key factor in Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me work through the eligibility assessment for Alex.

Since Alex is 6 years old, he falls into the "under 16" category. According to the rules, children under 16 generally qualify for Child Benefit, but I need to check a few more details to confirm.

Let me proceed with the next question:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This is just a standard check - at 6 years old, he's unlikely to be working, but I need to confirm this for the assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's only 6!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, at 6 years old this is unlikely, but I need to check)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(At 6 years old, this almost certainly won't apply, but I need to confirm for the assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that can qualify you - **any one of these would be sufficient**:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - you have a permanent home in the UK and spend most of your time here

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - you have permanently settled status

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for at least 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work (jobseeker status for up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family (and aren't claiming Income Support, JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit), OR
   - You're studying with sufficient financial resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - we're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. **Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - he lives with you at home (this seems to be the case based on what you've already told me)

2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - you pay towards his care, food, clothes, housing, or other living costs

3. **You're paying maintenance** - you make payments towards his maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, I assume option 1 applies - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else been claiming it for him recently?**

For example:
- His other parent
- A grandparent or other relative
- Another guardian

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex currently in any of these situations:**
- In hospital
- In local authority care
- Fostered
- Or living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're paying for his housing and upkeep yourself (not receiving support from the council for his care)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - I'm paying for everything myself. The council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you the outcome for Alex's eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me report your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

---

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for your 6-year-old son Alex:

✓ He is under 16 (a qualifying age)  
✓ He is not working full-time  
✓ He is not receiving benefits in his own right  
✓ He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✓ You are responsible for him and he lives with you  
✓ No one else is claiming for him  
✓ He is living normally at home  
✓ The council is not paying towards his care  

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Note:** If you or a partner earns over £60,000, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge (which reduces or removes the benefit)

### **Payment Information:**

- Payments are made every 4 weeks into your bank account
- If you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits, you can request weekly payments instead

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 6 years old (under 16), which is a qualifying age; (2) He is not working full-time; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK (Manchester); (6) You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you at home; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him; (8) He is living normally at home (not in hospital, care, or fostered); (9) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
